features.quote: a rock-cut reservoir (3.5 x 5.8 m) south of the site
features.subtype: rock-cut reservoir, 3.5 x 5.8 m, c. 3 m deep

date.basis: reservoir not dated itself; only the site is dated (sherds 2nd-3rd c. CE)

features.quote: The mouths of eight bell-shaped cisterns were identified on the site
features.subtype: bell-shaped rock-cut cisterns (eight in text, nine labels on plan)

date.basis: cisterns not dated individually; text says the (Roman-period) village's water supply relied on them

features.quote: About 20 m southeast of the site an almost intact sarcophagus
features.subtype: stone sarcophagus in situ, with lid

date.basis: sarcophagus not dated; attributed possibly to a Samaritan, no date given

notes: Plan Fig. 124 (p. 138) has a north arrow and 20 m bar but no grid or coordinates; the recorded point 201400/179800 (map ref 2014/1798, 100 m precision) cannot be placed on it, so no 'plan' positions. Cisterns: one entry for the group; the text gives no direction, so position 'none'. For information only (not coded): on Fig. 124 one 'Cistern' label lies in the northern part of the enclosure, c. 20 m north of the Tower that the text puts 'in the center of the village'; four lie in the eastern half, one west of the Tower, one just outside the south wall at its west end. Reservoir: south of the site per text; on the plan it lies just south of the Gate, outside the enclosure. Sarcophagus coded as a grave (burial container in situ), not a cavity with opening. No mouth relations stated. Dates: site sherds 2nd-3rd c. CE and 'fortified village in the Roman period' are site-level, so features take U. No absence statement.
